title: An account balance from sealed transactions

blocks.text: The page's domain-modeling example: a financial application has a sealed `Transaction` type with exactly three kinds, `Deposit`, `Withdrawal` and `Transfer`. `Ledger` models them as records of a sealed interface:
Write `static long balance(String account, List<Transaction> transactions)`: start at 0 and apply every transaction in order, as it affects `account`:

items: a deposit into `account` adds its cents;
a withdrawal from `account` takes its cents away;
a transfer takes its cents from `from` and adds them to `to`;
anything about other accounts does not change the balance.

blocks.text: Use a `switch` over the transaction; since `Transaction` is sealed, it needs no `default`. Balances may go negative.

cases.says: Deposits add to an account and withdrawals take from it.
Deposits and withdrawals for other accounts leave this account's balance alone.
A transfer takes from the paying account and adds to the receiving one.
A transfer from an account to itself leaves its balance unchanged.

concepts: A sealed type models a finite set of domain subtypes, such as deposit, withdrawal and transfer transactions.
